title: Time to Sunset Walk Planner: Beat the Dark
description: Plan an out-and-back walk that ends before dark with the Time to Sunset Walk Planner — sunset time, twilight buffer and walking range. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, with 90 minutes to sunset at a steady 5 km/h, your out-and-back turning point is about 3.75 km away — leave the return half in hand, then add twilight as your safety margin.
quick_answer: The Time to Sunset Walk Planner turns the time remaining until sunset into a walking plan: how far you can go and still return before dark, with civil twilight as buffer. Enter your start time and pace and read the turnaround point.
steps_intro: Half your remaining light is the way out. The planner enforces the rule:

Shoot the golden hour at the far point and walk back through civil twilight: the planner counts the twilight as usable buffer, labelled as such.
Unknown trails run slower than the map suggests; the planner's pace setting is where honesty about that goes.
Group pace is the slowest walker. Enter that pace and the plan forgives you.

90 minutes to sunset, 5 km/h pace: 7.5 km of total walking, so the turnaround sits at ~3.75 km. Arrive back at sunset, with civil twilight (roughly another 30 minutes of usable light at mid-latitudes) as unplanned insurance.
In December in London the whole post-lunch window can be 2 hours to a 15:53 sunset — the planner's winter answers are bracingly short, which is the point.

popular_table.title: How the plan is built
rows: Now until sunset (plus optional twilight buffer)
Your honest speed — 5 km/h (3.1 mph) is a fit adult on paths; trails run slower
Half the budget out, half back — the rule that cannot be argued with at dusk
Civil twilight after sunset, ~25–35 min at mid-latitudes, longer in summer
popular_table.note: Plans assume you can walk the return at the same pace in fading light. Headtorches remain excellent ideas regardless.

faq: As an optional buffer, clearly labelled — twilight is usable light for paths you know, not a promise on rough ground. The Civil Twilight Calculator prices your exact date's twilight.
Your slowest realistic pace for the terrain — 4 km/h on hills, 5 on paths, less with children. The plan is only as honest as this number.
If transport waits at the far end, the full budget is yours — the planner's out-and-back default is the conservative case; adjust the turnaround fraction consciously.
Why not walk back by moonlight?
Full-moon nights can be genuinely walkable — and the Next Full Moon Calculator will date them. The planner's job is the no-surprises baseline.
Overcast and canopy steal the last light early. Treat the twilight buffer as already spent in forests.
Sunset where — my location or the hilltop?
Computed for your position; a high viewpoint buys a few extra minutes (the Sun sets later uphill), a valley loses them.
The plan that needs no battery is the one on this page — glance, memorise the turnaround time, walk.
Double the pace and the same arithmetic holds — trail runners use this exact budget with a headtorch as the buffer's backup.
